question: Which vitamin is nearly absent from green coffee beans but made in quantity by roasting them?
answer: Niacin, vitamin B3. Green beans hold about 1% trigonelline, a bitter alkaloid; roasting heat strips a methyl group from it, leaving nicotinic acid, which is niacin. Light roasts carry about 10 mg per 100 g, very dark Italian roasts about 40 mg. A cup from 10 g of dark beans holds a few milligrams.
move: Processing can create a nutrient as well as destroy one.

diagram.caption: The darker the roast, the more trigonelline has turned into niacin.

source: Adrian & Frangne, Adv. Exp. Med. Biol., 1991
